decisions.statement: The commit is kept beside the page the deploy was read from.
A commit that was put up and a commit that refused are kept under two keys.
A deploy that refused keeps what it refused for beside that commit.
Every refusal one deploy answered is kept as one text, one to a line.
A refusal past four thousand characters is cut, and the cut says how long the whole was.
A page already keeping that commit is written to by nothing.
The commit is kept uncommitted, so keeping it lands no change.
A write that failed is answered as what went wrong rather than thrown.
Nothing here settles whether a deploy finished.
The moment a deploy ended is kept whether that deploy put up or refused.
A moment that will not parse is read as no moment rather than as the epoch.
A deploy that refused keeps that one moment under both the ending's key and the refusal's.
Which kind a deploy puts up settles where that deploy's commit is kept.
A workstation service's commit is kept beside its page in the checkout.
A workstation service's commit is read back from beside its page.
Nothing a workstation service's deploy keeps or reads here reaches a service.
A write beside the page that threw is answered as what went wrong.
Every other kind's commit is kept by a write handed to the pages rather than by writing the tree.
A write the pages refuse is what went wrong.
Every other kind's commit is read back by asking the pages for the page's values.
The page asked for is named by the page type and slug its path spells.
A moment a deploy kept is read back the way the commit is.

definition: what a deploy put up, what it refused at and for, and when it ended, beside the service's page
